acceptance.assertion: Fiji Locally Managed Marine Area Network and Nguna-Pele Marine and Land Protected Area Network are checked first against dated official or primary-near sources, with identity, governance role, operating-status claim, URL, retrieval date and source role recorded; another candidate may replace them only when the evidence is materially stronger.

A record is added only for a concrete community-governed marine or land-and-sea Commons identity; a donor, programme umbrella, historic project description or organization-wide impact claim is not substituted for the governed Commons itself.

Current operation is claimed only when dated object-specific evidence supports it. Historical continuity, a live parent website or undated programme text is insufficient; otherwise no active status is asserted and the batch may correctly end without a new catalogue entry.

No customary boundary, village, household, reef, spawning site, patrol route, protected-species location or other sensitive ecological or community location is reconstructed; any published geometry is a separately justified coarse island, province or country reference.

The task produces exactly one bounded outcome: either one source-reviewed Pacific island Commons addition with canonical and generated surfaces updated, or a checked result artifact explaining why no candidate met the evidence threshold; catalogue size is never used as a reason to lower the threshold.

Any catalogue change keeps canonical data, English presentation overlay, generated public shells, taxonomy projections, immutable release and delivery evidence synchronized, and passes full validation plus public browser smoke on the exact head.

Closeout binds the complete diff and exact head to review evidence, required CI, merge commit and production readback, or records a reviewed no-change result without opening a no-op implementation pull request.

approval.note: The user explicitly approved continuing Commonworld catalogue integration through Grabowski. Repository mutation is allowed only after one candidate passes the current identity, governance, activity, privacy and duplication checks; a reviewed no-addition result is valid.

goal: Qualify one current Pacific island marine Commons through primary-near source review, starting with Fiji LMMA Network and Nguna-Pele, add exactly one record only when current community-governance identity and safe public representation are sufficiently evidenced, and otherwise preserve catalogue quality with a reviewed no-addition result.
